steps.notes: Prompt-faithful impl (x<=0 -> sin(x)-1) FAILS all 3 tests; passes ONLY with the branch flipped to strict x<0 AND midpoint-formula node arithmetic. Target middle cell = +4/9 in all 3 tests; spec demands -4/9.
Passes with alpha_LF = 2 hardcoded (targets -0.75, 4.5, 22.5). Local/Rusanov alpha=max(|uL|,|uR|) gives -0.25 and 37.5 and fails tests 0/2; background pins '=2'.

Passes with dt=T/(n_t-1), n_t-1 Euler steps, ghost-copy free BC, alpha=2. Variant probe: dt=T/n_t, zero-ghost/periodic/extrapolation BC, and local alpha all FAIL -> tests well-constraining. n_x=31/21/11 give even cell counts, so the x=0 discontinuity sits on a vertex and this step is insulated from the 24.1 branch defect (passes with either branch choice).

findings.evidence: Prompt and main description both state the IC as 'sin(x)-1 for -pi/2 < x <= 0; sin(x)+1 for 0 < x < pi/2', so u(0) = sin(0)-1 = -1. All three tests (n_x = 10, 100, 30) have an ODD number of cells, so the middle cell is centered exactly at x=0, and the 3-point Gauss rule places its central node there (computes to exactly 0.0 in float64 for n=10 and n=30 with linspace/arange grids). The side nodes' contributions cancel by antisymmetry, so the middle cell average = (4/9)*u0(node). The frozen targets give +0.4444444444444444 = +4/9 for the middle cell in ALL THREE tests (indices 4, 49, 14), i.e. the gold evaluated u(0) = +1 — the 'x > 0' branch — contradicting the stated IC. Dynamic proof: steptest on impl_faithful.py (np.where(x <= 0, sin(x)-1, sin(x)+1), midpoint node arithmetic) -> 'RESULT step 24.1: FAIL (official joint scoring)'; identical code with the branch flipped to x < 0 -> PASS. Note the exact analytic cell average of the middle cell is 0 (neither +/-4/9), so an exact-integration solver fails too; the target encodes specifically 'Gauss quadrature with x=0 assigned to the positive branch'.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) regenerate the 24.1 targets with the stated branch assignment (middle cell becomes -4/9), or (b) change the IC statement to '-pi/2 < x < 0' / '0 <= x < pi/2' in both the step prompt and the main description, or (c) — cleanest — pick test n_x values with even cell counts (odd vertex counts, e.g. 11/31/101, as step 24.3 already does) so no quadrature node lands on the discontinuity.

findings.evidence: Because a Gauss node sits exactly on the discontinuity, the result is discontinuous in the node's last-bit rounding. Even the 'lucky' strict-x<0 implementation FAILS if the node is computed with the algebraically identical textbook affine map x_i + h*(t+1)/2 instead of the midpoint formula 0.5*(x_i + x_{i+1}): for n=10 the former rounds to -2.7755575615628914e-17 (< 0 -> wrong branch -> middle cell ~ -4/9) while the latter gives exactly 0.0. Verified: review/work/24/impl_flipped_v2map.py (x<0 branch + textbook map) -> 'RESULT step 24.1: FAIL (official joint scoring)'. So among four reasonable (branch x{<,<=}0) x (node-map) implementations, exactly ONE passes, and pass/fail hinges on invisible floating-point rounding rather than correctness.
findings.suggested_fix: Same root cause and same fix as the D7 finding: move the test grids to even cell counts so no quadrature node coincides with x=0; then all four implementation variants agree to ~1e-16 and the step scores robustly.

findings.evidence: Step description: 'Using maximum wave speed as the global Lax-Friedrichs stability parameter, alpha_LF.' The hardcoded value alpha_LF = 2 appears only in the step BACKGROUND ('alpha_LF = max||u|| = 2', valid for the IC range [-2,2]). Yet the tests feed inputs far outside that range: (uL,uR) = (3,3) and (5,-5), where the actual maximum wave speed is 5. A solver who reads 'maximum wave speed' as max(|uL|,|uR|) (the standard local LF / Rusanov flux) returns 37.5 for test 2 vs target 22.5 and -0.25 vs -0.75 for test 0, failing 2 of 3 tests. The word 'global' plus the background's explicit '= 2' disambiguate, so a careful solver passes, but in any evaluation setting where the background is withheld the step becomes a guess.
findings.suggested_fix: State 'use the fixed global value alpha_LF = 2 (the maximum wave speed of the initial condition)' in the step description or the function docstring, not only in the background; or use test inputs within [-2, 2] so the global and problem-consistent readings coincide.

findings.evidence: Garbled prompt text: 'The output will be cell-averaged values, an array of length n-The numerical integral should be performed with three-point Gauss quadrature rule.' — the '1.' after 'n-' was evidently lost in editing. Recoverable from the docstring ('v : ... 1d array size n-1'), so unlikely to flip scores.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the text to '...an array of length n-1. The numerical integral should be performed...'.

findings.evidence: Two doc inconsistencies: (1) step description has broken cross-references: 'using the initial conditon and Lax-Friedrichs functions from and .' (step numbers missing). (2) problem_io declares inputs 'a: left end... b: right end...' and output 'S : solution matrix, 2d array size (n_t-1) * (n_x-1)', but the scored contract is solve(n_x, n_t, T) returning 'u1 : solution vector, 1d array of size n_x-1'; the domain [-pi/2, pi/2] must be inferred from the IC support (the targets confirm it). The header docstring and tests are self-consistent, so a competent solver follows them.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the dangling 'from and .' references; align problem_io with the actual signature (drop a,b or state the fixed domain [-pi/2, pi/2]; output is the final 1d snapshot, not a 2d matrix).

overall_assessment: Steps 24.2 and 24.3 are fair and well-constrained: targets pin alpha_LF=2, dt=T/(n_t-1), and ghost-copy free BCs, and 24.3's even cell counts keep the discontinuity on a vertex. Step 24.1, however, is a blocker as-is: every test grid centers a cell on the x=0 discontinuity, putting a Gauss node exactly on it; the frozen targets encode u(0)=+1 while the prompt explicitly assigns x=0 to the sin(x)-1 branch (u(0)=-1), so a prompt-faithful solver fails all three tests, and even branch-flipped solvers fail under an algebraically equivalent node-mapping formula due to last-bit rounding. Regenerating 24.1's targets or moving its test grids to even cell counts fixes the problem completely.
